prompt: We had a church dinner. The roast beef and gravy were cooked the day before, left to cool overnight in a big stock pot on the counter, then reheated before serving. About 10-12 hours after the meal around 30 of the 40 guests had bad cramps and diarrhea, but hardly anyone vomited or had a fever. What most likely caused this and how do we stop it happening again?
assertions: Identifies Clostridium perfringens as the most likely cause
Explains that spores survive cooking and germinate/multiply rapidly during slow cooling or warm holding of the large pot
Explains it is a toxicoinfection: large numbers eaten, enterotoxin released when cells sporulate in the gut (not a preformed toxin)
Uses onset time and symptoms to rule out alternatives such as S. aureus or emetic B. cereus (rapid vomiting) and Salmonella (fever)
Gives specific cooling controls: shallow containers/portioning, ice bath or fridge so food cools quickly through the danger zone
Gives holding/reheating controls: hot hold at or above about 140 F (60 C) and reheat to about 165 F (74 C)
